Timeline::max¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::max(bool skipna = true) const

Find The Latest Valid Instant¶

max() searches the entire Timeline and returns the latest valid timestamp as a scalar Timeline. All dimensions participate in one reduction, so the result has shape=[] regardless of receiver rank. The method has no axis-wise or shape-retaining overload.

skipna controls NaT propagation:

  • true (the default) excludes NaT and returns the latest valid instant.

  • false returns scalar NaT if any input element is NaT.

Chronology is determined from absolute epoch nanoseconds. Input order, formatted timezone offsets, and duplicates do not affect which instant is greatest. max() does not reorder or mutate the receiver.

Absent-Instant Rule¶

With skipna=true, NaT positions are ignored whenever at least one valid instant exists. An empty or all-NaT receiver returns scalar NaT. Use isnat_scalar() when an absent maximum must trigger fallback or validation logic.

Example 1: Reduce Every Matrix Element¶

const auto observations = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2025-06-15T08:30:00Z", ""},
    {"2024-01-02T18:45:00Z", "2026-09-30T03:15:00Z"},
});

pluss::timeline::print(std::cout, observations.max());

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[], tz=UTC)
2026-09-30 03:15:00

The result is one scalar, not one maximum per row or column. The receiver remains [2,2] after the call.

Example 2: Duplicates Do Not Change The Value¶

const auto duplicated = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2025-06-15T08:30:00Z",
    "2024-01-02T18:45:00Z",
    "2026-09-30T03:15:00Z",
    "2026-09-30T03:15:00Z",
});

pluss::timeline::print(std::cout, duplicated.max());

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[], tz=UTC)
2026-09-30 03:15:00

Both latest entries represent the same value. Because max() returns the timestamp rather than its position, tie order is intentionally irrelevant.

Example 3: Empty And All-NaT Inputs¶

const auto absent = pluss::timeline::make({"", ""});
const auto empty =
    pluss::timeline::from_epoch(std::vector<std::int64_t>{});

pluss::timeline::print(std::cout, absent.max());
std::cout << '\n';
pluss::timeline::print(std::cout, empty.max());

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[], tz=UTC)
NaT
Timeline(shape=[], tz=UTC)
NaT

Example 4: Preserve The Receiver Timezone¶

const auto utc = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2025-06-15T08:30:00Z",
    "2024-01-02T18:45:00Z",
    "2026-09-30T03:15:00Z",
});
const auto local = utc.tz_convert("America/New_York");

pluss::timeline::print(std::cout, local.max());

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[], tz=America/New_York)
2026-09-29 23:15:00

The local date is September 29 even though the UTC rendering is September 30. Both identify the same latest instant; timezone retention changes presentation and local calendar fields, not ordering.

Example 5: Propagate Any NaT¶

const auto observations = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2025-06-15T08:30:00Z", "",
    "2026-09-30T03:15:00Z",
});

pluss::timeline::print(std::cout, observations.max(false));

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[], tz=UTC)
NaT

This mode is useful when “latest” is meaningful only for a complete set of observations.

Choosing The Right Operation¶

  • Use max() for the latest valid timestamp value.

  • Use argsort() when the winning position matters.

  • Use sort() when later work needs the complete chronological sequence.

  • Do not confuse the maximum with the last stored element in unsorted data.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Reduction is global; no dimension argument is accepted.

  • NaT is skipped by default and propagated when skipna=false.

  • The returned timezone matches the receiver.

  • The scalar result remains a Timeline, so calendar extraction, formatting, and timezone conversion remain available.

Summary¶

max() means “latest valid instant over all elements.” It returns a scalar, retains timezone and nanosecond identity, ignores NaT positions by default, can propagate them on request, and leaves the source Timeline unchanged.

See Also¶

  • min: return the earliest valid instant.

  • argsort: obtain chronological positions.

  • isnat_scalar: detect an absent maximum.
